title: Kentucky Sales Tax Guide: Rates, Taxability, & Compliance
summary: Kentucky sales tax is a flat 6% with no local rates. Learn what’s taxable, how to register for a permit, and when to file returns.
body_markdown:
## Kentucky sales tax at a glance


**State taxing authority** Kentucky Department of Revenue


**Kentucky sales tax rate** 6%


**Local sales tax rates** N/A


**Combined sales tax rate** 6%


**Economic nexus threshold** $100,000 or more in gross receipts from the current or previous calendar year


**Website**[revenue.ky.gov](https://revenue.ky.gov/)


**Tax line** 502-564-4581


Kentucky has a single[statewide sales tax rate of 6%](https://revenue.ky.gov/Business/Sales-Use-Tax/pages/default.aspx) . The state has no additional local sales taxes from city or county governments or special tax districts.


Kentucky taxes most tangible personal property with sales tax. Kentucky also taxes “[prewritten computer software access services](https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/statutes/statute.aspx?id=58185) ,” or SaaS, as well as digital products like audiobooks and video games.


Kentucky’s economic nexus threshold for retailers is[$100,000 or more in gross receipts](https://revenue.ky.gov/News/Publications/Sales%20Tax%20Newsletters/Sales%20Tax%20Facts%20-%20Summer%202026.pdf) from the current or previous calendar year. Effective[Aug. 1, 2026](https://revenue.ky.gov/News/Publications/Sales%20Tax%20Newsletters/Sales%20Tax%20Facts%20-%20Summer%202026.pdf) , Kentucky no longer has a transaction-count threshold for economic nexus.

## Kentucky sales tax rates and calculations


Kentucky’s sales tax rate is a flat 6% statewide, with no local taxes. This means the sales tax rate stays the same regardless of where in the state the purchase happened, making sales tax calculations straightforward.


### How to calculate Kentucky sales tax


To calculate sales tax in Kentucky, multiply the item’s purchase price by the 6% state sales tax rate.


For example, if you’re selling an item for $50, your sales tax calculation would look like this:


**$50 x 0.06 = $3**


Then add the sales tax to the item's purchase price, so the customer pays $53 (plus any other applicable fees).


### Origin vs. destination sourcing in Kentucky


Kentucky uses[destination-based sourcing](https://www.numeral.com/blog/origin-based-vs-destination-based-sales-tax) when calculating sales tax on remote purchases. This means that the tax rate is applied based on where the buyer receives the product, not where the seller is located.


For example, if a buyer in Kentucky buys online from a seller in New York, they would pay Kentucky’s flat 6% tax rate instead of New York’s state and local taxes.


### Is Kentucky a Streamlined Sales Tax state?


Yes, Kentucky is a full member of the[Streamlined Sales and Use Tax Agreement](https://www.streamlinedsalestax.org/) . This agreement simplifies the registration, filing, and remittance process for remote sellers with customers in multiple member states.


## Sales tax nexus in Kentucky


[Nexus](https://www.numeral.com/blog/sales-tax-nexus) is a legal connection between your business and a state that requires you to collect and remit sales tax there.


There are four main types of sales tax nexus:


- **Physical:** The business has a physical presence in the state, such as a retail store, warehouse, office, or remote employees. Learn more with Numeral’s[physical nexus guide](https://www.numeral.com/blog/physical-nexus) .
- **Economic:** The business has reached a sales volume or transaction count threshold in the state. Learn more with Numeral’s[economic nexus guide](https://www.numeral.com/blog/economic-nexus) .
- **Affiliate:** The business is legally affiliated with another organization in the state, such as a sister company or subsidiary.
- **Marketplace:** The business sells to customers in the state through an online marketplace like Amazon, eBay, or Etsy. Learn more with Numeral’s[marketplace facilitator guide](https://www.numeral.com/blog/marketplace-facilitator) .


Even if your business isn’t based in Kentucky, you could still have nexus there by making remote sales or having another existing legal connection. If you sell remotely into Kentucky, you’ll need to monitor your activity in the state so you know when you’re approaching nexus.


Numeral offers[free nexus monitoring](https://www.numeral.com/product/nexus-tracking) to help you stay on top of your state tax obligations.


Each state has its own sales tax nexus thresholds. Here are the current[nexus thresholds in Kentucky](https://www.numeral.com/nexus/kentucky) :


**Physical** Any physical presence or operational footprint in the state, including an office, store, warehouse, full- or part-time employees, or inventory stored in a third-party warehouse


**Economic** $100,000 or more in gross receipts during the current or previous calendar year


**Affiliate** The business operates indirectly through a subsidiary, related entity, representative, or agent in the state


**Marketplace** Marketplace providers with economic nexus in Kentucky are[required to collect and remit sales taxes on behalf of their sellers](https://taxanswers.ky.gov/Sales-and-Excise-Taxes/Pages/Remote-Retailers-Marketplace-Providers-FAQs.aspx)


Until[Aug. 1, 2026](https://revenue.ky.gov/News/Publications/Sales%20Tax%20Newsletters/Sales%20Tax%20Facts%20-%20Summer%202026.pdf) , remote sellers also had economic nexus if they made 200 or more separate transactions into Kentucky. A change to state law removed that test, so gross receipts now determine economic nexus.


If you only sell products in Kentucky through a marketplace platform like Amazon, you are not required to file and remit state sales tax yourself. The marketplace provider is required to handle sales taxes for you.


However, if you make both direct sales and marketplace sales in Kentucky, you’ll need to collect and remit sales taxes yourself on the direct sales once you hit the state’s economic nexus threshold.


In this situation, both direct sales and marketplace sales count toward the economic nexus threshold, even though you’re only required to collect and remit taxes on direct sales.


## What’s taxable and exempt in Kentucky


Most tangible personal property is subject to sales tax in Kentucky, with a few notable exemptions. SaaS subscriptions and digital products are generally taxable, too.


Here’s an overview of what’s taxable and exempt in Kentucky.


Category Generally taxable? Notes


Tangible personal property Yes Notable exemption for required textbooks for courses at nonprofit schools, colleges, and universities


Groceries No Unprepared food and ingredients are exempt from sales tax


Clothing Yes No sales tax holidays or exemptions for clothing purchases


Prescription drugs No Some qualifying medical devices and prosthetics are also exempt


SaaS Yes Prewritten computer software access services are taxable


Digital goods Yes Digital versions of required educational textbooks are exempt


Services Varies Only services listed in state law are taxable; the list has grown since 2022


Shipping Yes Shipping charges are generally taxable if the underlying product is taxable


### What is subject to sales tax in Kentucky


Most purchases in Kentucky are subject to sales tax, including:


- Tangible personal property
- Prepared foods, candy, tobacco, and alcohol
- Clothing
- SaaS
- Digital goods
- Services listed in state law, such as landscaping, pet care, and photography
- Shipping and handling charges


In 2022 and 2023, Kentucky amended[state law](https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/statutes/statute.aspx?id=58186) to significantly expand the number of[taxable service categories](https://www.numeral.com/blog/sales-tax-on-services) . Many services previously exempt from sales tax are now taxable.


### What’s exempt from sales tax in Kentucky


Some purchases are exempt from Kentucky state sales tax. These include:


- Groceries
- Prescription medication
- Qualifying medical devices and prosthetics
- [Required textbooks](https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/statutes/statute.aspx?id=57938) for courses at nonprofit schools, colleges, and universities
- [Agricultural supplies](https://revenue.ky.gov/DOR%20Training%20Materials/103%20KAR%2030.091.%20Sales%20to%20farmers.pdf)
- [Residential utility bills](https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/statutes/statute.aspx?id=58191)
- [Some services](https://revenue.ky.gov/News/Publications/Sales%20Tax%20Newsletters/Sales%20Tax%20Facts%202022%20-%20Sep.pdf) , including necessary medical services, educational services, financial and legal services, videography, and hairdressing


### SaaS and digital goods taxability in Kentucky


[SaaS is broadly taxable in Kentucky](https://www.numeral.com/blog/saas-sales-tax-kentucky) . Kentucky amended its state law in 2022 to tax “prewritten computer software access services,” effective[Jan. 1, 2023](https://revenue.ky.gov/News/Publications/Sales%20Tax%20Newsletters/Sales%20Tax%20Facts%202022%20-%20Jun.pdf) , which includes SaaS subscriptions.


Kentucky also taxes prewritten software when it's downloaded. Custom software can be treated differently, including separately stated charges for custom modifications.


Kentucky also broadly taxes[digital goods](https://www.numeral.com/blog/sales-tax-on-digital-goods) . This includes downloadable music, movies, games, books, and art. Kentucky taxes digital property even when the buyer's access is temporary or depends on continued payment.


### Resale and exemption certificates in Kentucky


[Exemption certificates](https://www.numeral.com/blog/sales-tax-exemption-certificates) , including[resale certificates](https://www.numeral.com/blog/resale-certificates) , exempt you from paying sales tax on an item if you plan to resell it.


To get an exemption certificate in Kentucky, you’ll first need to register and get a Sales and Use Tax Permit from the state’s Department of Revenue.


Then, you’ll need to fill out one of the three exemption certificate forms accepted in Kentucky. These are:


- Kentucky Resale Certificate ([Form 51A105](https://revenue.ky.gov/Forms/51A105%20%287-19%29.pdf) )
- Streamlined Sales Tax (SST) Exemption Certificate ([Form 51A260](https://revenue.ky.gov/Forms/KY%20Form%2051A260%20%2812-21%29%20exemption%20certificate.pdf) )
- Multistate Tax Commission (MTC)[Uniform Sales & Use Tax Resale Certificate](https://www.mtc.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/Unif-Resale-Cert-revised-10-14-22.pdf)


If your business operates in multiple states, the SST or MTC exemption certificate may be the most efficient option.


After completing your exemption certificate, present it directly to your suppliers to claim the sales tax exemption. You do not need to submit your exemption certificate to the Kentucky state government.


[Kentucky exemption certificates do not expire](https://www.numeral.com/blog/sales-tax-exemption-certificate-expiration-by-state) as long as your Sales and Use Tax Permit is active. However, you will need to complete a new resale certificate if your business changes significantly, such as changing your name or address.


Businesses should keep their exemption certificates on hand for[at least four years](https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/statutes/statute.aspx?id=49181) after each purchase where they’re used. This helps protect your business in a sales tax audit.


If you’re looking for help tracking your exemption certificates, check out[Numeral’s exemption certificate management product](https://www.numeral.com/product/exemption-certificate-management) .


## Registering for a Kentucky sales and use tax permit


You need to[register for a Kentucky Sales and Use Tax Permit](https://www.numeral.com/sales-tax-registration/kentucky) to collect, file, and remit sales tax in Kentucky.


To get started, first create an account on Kentucky’s[MyTaxes portal](https://mytaxes.ky.gov/) to manage Kentucky sales tax and other state taxes online. Then complete the[Kentucky Tax Registration Application](https://revenue.ky.gov/Business/pages/register-business.aspx) through MyTaxes.


You can also register using the[paper application](https://revenue.ky.gov/Forms/10A100%28P%29%284-25%29_FINAL_locked%20Fill-in.pdf) , but processing and approval take longer. Either way, indicate that you’re applying for a Sales and Use Tax Permit.


On the application, you’ll need to provide information about your business, including:


- Legal business name
- Business address
- Business structure
- FEIN or SSN
- Owners’ names
- Owners’ contact information
- NAICS industry code


Registering for a Kentucky Sales and Use Tax Permit is free. Permits don’t expire or need renewal; they stay active until you cancel them.


### Registration requirements for remote sellers


Remote sellers that have met Kentucky’s economic nexus for sales tax can either register for a Kentucky Sales and Use Tax Permit or register through the[Streamlined Sales Tax Registration System](https://www.streamlinedsalestax.org/for-businesses/sales-tax-registration-sstrs) .


If you choose a Kentucky Sales and Use Tax Permit, the process is the same as for an in-state seller.


If you register through Streamlined Sales Tax, you’ll be assigned an ID number to collect and remit sales tax in member states. You’ll need to provide business and tax details during registration. Registration is free and never expires, but you can opt to cancel it.


If you opt to register through Streamlined Sales Tax, you’ll still have to collect and remit taxes directly to the Kentucky Department of Revenue. You’ll also be required to collect and remit taxes to every other state you registered with, even if you don’t otherwise have nexus in those states.


## Collecting Kentucky sales tax


Once you’ve registered for a Kentucky Sales and Use Tax Permit, you’ll need to start collecting sales tax on all taxable purchases.


For each transaction, determine whether it's taxable and confirm the buyer is located in Kentucky. Then apply the 6% sales tax rate to the transaction and collect the tax as part of the purchase.


Many ecommerce platforms and point-of-sale systems include features that automatically calculate and collect sales tax for each purchase. Be sure to track all sales tax collected for future filing and reporting.


### Marketplace sales


In Kentucky,[marketplace providers](https://www.numeral.com/blog/marketplace-facilitator) need to handle sales tax on behalf of their sellers. This includes collecting, tracking, filing, and remitting these taxes. Retailers that sell only in Kentucky through online marketplaces do not need to collect and remit their own sales taxes.


However, retailers who make both marketplace sales and direct sales still need to collect and remit taxes on their direct sales. When filing returns, these retailers must report and deduct marketplace sales.


Retailers making both direct and marketplace sales also need to register for a Kentucky Sales and Use Tax Permit. In this situation, both marketplace sales and direct sales count toward economic nexus.


### Shipping and delivery charges


Under Kentucky state law,[shipping, delivery, and handling charges](https://www.numeral.com/blog/sales-tax-on-shipping) are generally subject to sales tax as long as the underlying product being shipped is taxable. If the product being shipped is tax-exempt, the shipping charges are not taxable either.


## Filing and paying Kentucky sales tax


[To file and remit sales tax in Kentucky](https://www.numeral.com/blog/how-to-file-kentucky-sales-tax-online) , use the state’s[MyTaxes portal](https://mytaxes.ky.gov/) . Kentucky[no longer accepts paper sales tax returns](https://revenue.ky.gov/News/Pages/Online-Filing-and-Payment-Mandate-for-Sales-and-Excise-Tax-Returns.aspx) .


For most businesses, sales tax returns must be[filed monthly](https://taxanswers.ky.gov/Sales-and-Excise-Taxes/Pages/Sales-and-Excise-Tax-FAQs.aspx) . However, some businesses may qualify for less frequent filing schedules if they have a lower annual tax liability. You can request a quarterly or annual filing frequency by contacting the Kentucky Department of Revenue directly.


Sales tax returns are[due on the 20th of the month](https://www.numeral.com/blog/sales-tax-due-dates) following the reporting period. If the 20th is on a weekend or holiday, returns are due on the next business day.


Your business must file a return for every reporting period, even if you made zero sales or collected zero sales tax in Kentucky.


Failing to file returns could trigger penalties. If your business is no longer active, you’ll need to formally close your Sales and Use Tax Permit and file a final return to avoid future penalties.


Kentucky offers vendor compensation for filing tax returns on time. When collecting and remitting taxes on time, vendors can deduct[1.75% of the first $1,000 due](https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/statutes/statute.aspx?id=42624) and 1.5% of the remaining tax due, up to $50 total.


## Kentucky sales tax penalties and interest


Failing to file and remit your Kentucky state taxes on time can come with[penalties and interest](https://revenue.ky.gov/Collections/Pages/Penalties-Interest-and-Fees.aspx) .


Late filing incurs a penalty of 2% of the total tax due for each 30-day period the return is late, up to a maximum of 20% of the total tax due.


Late payments also incur a penalty of 2% of the total tax due for each 30-day period the payment is late. Late payment penalties have a minimum of $10 and a maximum of 20% of the total tax due.


Late payments may also incur a 25% collection fee on unpaid tax due 60 days after the original notice date.


Kentucky also charges interest on late tax payments, which can change annually. The 2026[interest rate is 9%](https://revenue.ky.gov/News/Pages/Tax-Interest-Rate-Update-for-01-01-26.aspx) .


## Kentucky sales tax recordkeeping and audits


The Kentucky Department of Revenue may[audit](https://www.numeral.com/blog/sales-tax-audit) your sales taxes to confirm that your returns were correct. They may evaluate:


- Reported sales
- Taxability
- Exemptions
- Tax collected
- Tax remitted


Kentucky can audit businesses for up to four years after their sales tax returns were due or filed, whichever is later. Businesses are legally required to maintain their sales tax records for at least four years, but it may be helpful to keep records for longer.


Businesses should maintain the following records:


- Sales tax returns
- Resale and exemption certificates
- General financial records documenting sales and returns


You can appeal a Kentucky state sales tax audit by submitting a[written protest](https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/statutes/statute.aspx?id=53106) of a Notice of Tax Due within 60 days.

## Kentucky sales tax FAQs


**What is the sales tax rate in Kentucky?**
Kentucky’s state sales tax rate is 6%. Kentucky has no local tax rates.


**What is the economic nexus threshold in Kentucky?**
Kentucky’s economic nexus threshold for sales tax is $100,000 in gross receipts during the current or previous calendar year.


**Is SaaS taxable in Kentucky?**
Yes, SaaS is generally taxable in Kentucky.


**Do I need a sales tax permit in Kentucky?**
Yes, sellers with nexus in Kentucky need a Kentucky Sales and Use Tax Permit. You can register either directly with the Kentucky Department of Revenue or through the Streamlined Sales Tax system.


**How often do businesses need to file sales tax returns in Kentucky?**
Most Kentucky businesses must file sales tax returns monthly. Businesses with low sales tax liability may request a quarterly or annual filing schedule by contacting the Kentucky Department of Revenue directly.
